summary.intent: Update the codebase map (CONCERNS.md, STRUCTURE.md) to reflect completed phases 28-33, clean up stale planning docs, and plan Phase 34 for E2E test expansion.
summary.outcome: Updated and merged two PRs: codebase map refresh (PR #390) and docs cleanup including DEFERRED.md, ROADMAP.md Phase 34 addition, and security backlog audit (PR #391). Phase 34 research completed and planning in progress on branch test/phase-34-e2e-expansion.

repo: Phase 28 replaced all 127 console.* calls in the web app with a structured logger at apps/web/src/lib/logger.ts, but web3auth/hooks.ts still has 12 unguarded console.time/timeEnd calls
registerFaroTransport() is defined in the Grafana Faro setup but never called, meaning logger.error/warn calls do not reach Faro
Phase 31 decomposed useSharedNavigation.ts (1199→378 lines) and FileBrowser.tsx (964→362 lines); folder.service.ts (1059 lines) and bin.service.ts (971 lines) remain large
Phase 32 resolved the FUSE FilePointer sync-blocking issue on macOS; Phase 33 completed the Windows equivalent using rt.spawn() channel patterns
The legacy POC directory was removed in commit ee9bcd4e4 (Phase 28) — any references to it in planning docs are stale
Batch download in handleBatchDownload (useFileBrowserActions.ts:430-446) downloads files individually via downloadFromIpns — there is no zip generation despite todo description saying otherwise
CTR streaming mode requires BOTH STREAMING_MIME_TYPES membership AND file.size > 256KB to trigger service worker interception
Media preview dialogs (Video, Audio, PDF) use CSS class selectors only (.video-player-modal etc.) with no data-testid attributes
BYO-IPFS load test execution remains infrastructure-blocked — no external IPFS provider set up for staging, same constraint as Phase 21
FUSE production code has 19+ mutex lock().unwrap() sites that can cause cascading panics on mutex poisoning
The Entire CLI injects git hooks (.husky/post-commit, pre-push, prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg.pre-entire) as local artifacts that are not in .gitignore
192.168.133.114 (docker host IP) appeared in 15 planning doc files across 30 occurrences — was sanitized to <docker-host>
All 7 low-severity Phase 9 security backlog items (#13-19) were resolved organically in later phases without being marked done in LOW-SEVERITY-BACKLOG.md
